title: THE PEOPLE COME TO SEEK GOD'S WILL

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Moses answered him, 'Because the people come to me to seek God's will. Whenever
they have a dispute, it is brought to me, and I decide between the parties and
inform them of God's decrees and instructions.'" - Ex 18:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses gives his reason, and it is a good one. The people come seeking God's will.
He is teaching them God's decrees. This is genuine spiritual work.

Notice that Moses does not defend himself with pride. He simply explains. He
believes he is doing what needs to be done.

And here is the difficulty: he was right about the work and wrong about the
method. The teaching mattered. The disputes needed settling. But it did not
follow that he had to do all of it himself.

We often confuse those two things. Because a task is important, we assume we
must be the one to do it. Sometimes that is true. Often it is not, and our
assumption quietly prevents other people from developing.

There may also be something else at work in situations like this, and it is
worth naming gently. Being the person everyone needs can become part of how we
see ourselves. Letting go of that is not merely a scheduling change; it touches
identity.

Moses answers honestly, and he listens to what comes next. That is to his great
credit.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What are you doing that someone else could do, perhaps not as well, but well
   enough?
2. Is any part of your identity tied up in being needed?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, show me where I have confused a task being important with it being mine.
Free me from needing to be indispensable. Amen.
